trigger: reading the changelog fragment and the 38db91727 commit message
summary: The changelog fragment and the 38db91727 commit message say the agent stayed unreconnected until the update interval elapsed; the old loop never exited on teardown, so the stall was unbounded, not interval-bounded. Raised independently by security-guardian and docs-writer in the same Gate 2 wave; compliance-officer, enterprise-readiness and sre also noted it.
classification_rationale: the prose contradicts the code behaviour it describes (old loop waited on the AgentImpl stop flag and never exited on a reconnect teardown)

trigger: an operator upgrading a fleet whose agents are already wedged on the old update thread
summary: The changelog fragment gives no recovery step for agents already wedged before the fix is installed. sre raised the same gap in the same wave.

trigger: --update-check-interval set to 0 or a negative value (no CLI validator, main.cpp:443)
summary: An interval <= 0 makes check_and_apply spin with no wait; the old loop spun the same way. Also raised by cpp-expert and sre (UP-6 in the unhappy-path register is the same defect).
classification_rationale: the option accepts values the loop cannot honour; no wording is involved

trigger: --update-check-interval larger than roughly 9.2e9 seconds, so wait_for computes now() + ceil<steady_clock::duration>(interval) and overflows
summary: A huge interval overflows the wait_for deadline computation (undefined behaviour). The old loop subtracted in seconds, so the new wait_for makes it reachable. I5 was considered by the reporter if the overflow wraps into a spin; recorded I8 as the base case.
classification_rationale: an accepted option value produces undefined behaviour in the new wait

trigger: AgentImpl::run() throws between the update-thread spawn (agent.cpp:2117) and the join (agent.cpp:3339), so the stub unique_ptr unwinds before the ScopeExit quiesce_run_workers() joins the thread
summary: The update thread may still be inside check_and_apply(raw_stub) on a destroyed stub after an exception unwind; the old code has the same shape. unhappy-path recorded the same defect as UP-9.
classification_rationale: the lifetime the surrounding comments rely on (stub outlives the update thread) does not hold on the exception path

trigger: the first new updater test sleeps 200ms and assumes the loop is parked
summary: The 200ms sleep does not guarantee the loop is parked in the wait. Not a false green: a regression still fails the 5s bound.
classification_rationale: a test-robustness nit; the test still fails on the regression it guards
